'''Solyanka''' ({{langx|ru|соля́нка}}; initially ''selyanka''; {{langx|ru|селя́нка}}, {{IPA|ru|sɐˈlʲankə|}}) is a thick and sour [[soup]] of [[Russian cuisine|Russian]] origin.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Sinclair |first1=Charles |title=A Cook's Dictionary: International Food and Cooking Terms from A to Z |date=October 2005 |publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing Plc |isbn=978-1-904970-18-7 |page=540 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/A_Cook_s_Dictionary/oC08NQAACAAJ?hl=en |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Bender |first1=David A. |title=A Dictionary of Food and Nutrition |date=29 January 2009 |publisher=OUP Oxford |isbn=978-0-19-157975-2 |page=497 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/2DYLeaWedK0C |language=en |quote=Russian; fish or meat stew with salted or pickled vegetables}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Smith |first1=Alison K. |title=Recipes for Russia: Food and Nationhood under the Tsars |date=26 February 2008 |publisher=Cornell University Press |isbn=978-1-5017-5745-7 |pages=160,186 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Recipes_for_Russia/af_-DwAAQBAJ |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Kelly |first1=Catriona |title=Russian Food since 1800: Empire at Table |date=8 February 2024 |publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing |isbn=978-1-350-19280-5 |page=25 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Russian_Food_since_1800/4SPsEAAAQBAJ |language=en}}</ref> It is a common dish in [[Russia]], [[Ukraine]], [[Belarus]], the [[Baltic states]],<ref>{{cite book |last=Zak |first=Zuza |title=Amber & Rye: A Baltic Food Journey |year=2021 |publisher=[[Interlink Books]] |isbn=978-1-62-371900-5 |page=94 |quote=Originating in Russia, solyanka gets its name from its saltiness. With the Baltic States having been part of the Soviet Union for so long, there is a clear overlap in terms of cuisine and culture.}}</ref> and other [[post-Soviet states]] and other parts of the former [[Eastern Bloc]]. It was one of the most reliably available dishes in [[East Germany]] ({{langx|de|Soljanka}}).<ref name="Heinzelmann"/>
